✓ See lightning → count to thunder
✓ Every 3 seconds = 1km
✓ If < 30 sec (< 10km): VERY CLOSE, stay indoors

ADVICE FOR PRE-PERIOD:
→ Extreme heat: Skip outdoors, stay cool
→ Hydration: 2.5L water
→ Be kind to yourself

OVULATION (Days 12-16):
Energy: PEAK (best time for exercise, sports)
Heat tolerance: Moderate
Mood: Positive

ADVICE FOR OVULATION:
→ Best time for outdoor exercise
→ Go for picnic, sports, adventure
→ Peak energy window

PRACTICAL TIPS:
✓ Track cycle: Use app (Flo, Clue)
✓ Plan activities: Know good vs hard days
✓ Bathroom access: Know locations
✓ Carry: Pads, wipes, extra undergarments

sops.name: Frostbite Risk Alert
sops.regional_context: Shimla, Manali, higher elevations Jan-Feb
sops.why_this_sop: Severe cold causes rapid frostbite, tissue damage
sops.advice_template:
Temperature is {temperature_2m}°C — severe frostbite risk.

FROSTBITE TIMELINE:
✓ 0 to -5°C: 30-60 min before frostbite
✓ -5 to -15°C: 10-30 min
✓ Below -15°C: 5-10 min (CRITICAL)

PROTECTION:
✓ Clothing: 3-4 layers (thermal base → middle → windproof jacket)
✓ Extremities: Insulated gloves, wool socks, waterproof boots, face mask/balaclava
✓ Exposed skin: Apply cream/oil (barrier against wind)

OUTDOOR LIMIT:
✓ < -5°C: Max 20 min continuous
✓ < -10°C: Max 10 min, then 10 min warmth
✓ < -15°C: Only 5 min, then must warm up

FROSTBITE RECOGNITION:
✓ Stage 1: Skin pale/white, tingling, loss of sensation
✓ Stage 2: Blistering, severe pain when warming
✓ Stage 3: Black tissue (permanent damage)

TREATMENT:
✓ Move indoors immediately
✓ Warm gradually (NOT rapid = tissue damage)
✓ Warm drink (warm body from inside)
✓ Go to hospital (severe frostbite = amputation risk)

✓ Short-faced breeds (Bulldogs, Pugs) most at risk

PET SAFETY:
✓ KEEP INDOORS (AC room, cool space)
✓ Provide water constantly (change every 2 hours, heat warms it)
✓ Frozen water bowl (ice keeps it cool longer)
✓ Wet towel in cool corner (pet can lie on it if overheating)
✓ NO walks today (even brief ones dangerous)
✓ NO exercise (wait until evening)

OUTDOOR NECESSITIES (Bathroom only):
✓ Early morning: 5:30-7 AM (coolest)
✓ Late evening: 7-9 PM
✓ Avoid hot pavement (check with hand; if too hot for you, too hot for paws)
✓ Keep walks short (5-10 min max)
✓ Carry water (for drinking)

HOME SETUP:
✓ AC running (pets need AC in heat)
✓ Fans (air circulation)
✓ Shaded windows (block direct sun)
✓ Ventilation: Don't close all windows (ensure airflow)
✓ Hydration: Water bowls in multiple rooms

HEAT STRESS SIGNS:
✓ Excessive panting (not normal)
✓ Drooling
✓ Lethargy (lying down, won't get up)
✓ Reluctance to walk
✓ Vomiting, diarrhea
✓ Collapse (EMERGENCY)

TREATMENT:
✓ Get to cool place immediately
✓ Wet cloth on body (cool gradually, not ice cold)
✓ Offer water (don't force)
✓ Call vet if symptoms persist

sops.name: Pregnant Women All-Weather Safety
sops.description: Pregnancy-specific weather risks across all conditions
sops.regional_context: Bengaluru, all seasons
sops.why_this_sop: Pregnancy changes body's weather tolerance significantly
sops.advice_template:
You're pregnant. Weather affects pregnancy differently:

HEAT (> 38°C):
✓ Core temp higher in pregnancy = feels hotter
✓ Hydration: 3-4L water daily
✓ Activity: Slow walks only, max 30 min
✓ Medical: Inform doctor before going out
✓ Warning: Dizziness, cramps, reduced fetal movement = STOP, call doctor

COLD (< 10°C):
✓ Wear warm layers (core temp matters for baby)
✓ Avoid slipping (balance already off)
✓ Keep moving (staying still = body loses heat faster)

RAIN:
✓ Avoid slipping (poor balance in pregnancy)
✓ Use handrails/walls
✓ Waterproof shoes with grip
✓ Don't go out if raining heavily

LIGHTNING:
✓ Get indoors immediately
✓ Avoid stress (stress hormones affect fetus)

HUMIDITY (> 80%):
✓ Swelling worse (feet, hands, face)
✓ Heat feels worse (can't cool efficiently)
✓ Stay indoors, AC essential

GENERAL:
✓ Check with doctor: Is today's weather safe for me?
✓ Afternoon rest: 2 hours after lunch
✓ Hydration: Drink before thirst (thirst = dehydrated)
✓ Inform someone: Tell family when going out, ETA back
✓ Fetal monitoring: Know fetal movement pattern
  - Reduced movement in heat/stress = call doctor

sops.name: Hailstorm & Hail Damage Alert
sops.regional_context: Pre-monsoon (Mar-May) N & Central India, Vidarbha, MP, Maharashtra; occasional interior Karnataka. Damages crops, vehicles, injures people.
sops.why_this_sop: Hail causes rapid crop loss, vehicle denting, and head injury in the open; distinct from ordinary rain.
sops.advice_template:
Hail is indicated by the current weather code ({weather_code}). Take cover NOW.
IMMEDIATE:
- Get indoors / under solid roof; stay away from windows and skylights
- Move vehicles under cover; if driving, pull over safely, avoid trees and hoardings
- Do NOT shelter under trees or temporary structures
FARMERS:
- Cover/secure standing produce and livestock if safe to do so
AFTER:
- Wait for the all-clear before returning outdoors; hail often precedes lightning
sops.traceable_to_api: weather_code from /current (WMO 96 = thunderstorm w/ slight hail, 99 = heavy hail)

sops.name: Dense Fog & Low Visibility Alert
sops.regional_context: Indo-Gangetic plain (Delhi, UP, Punjab, Bihar) Dec-Jan. Causes highway pile-ups, flight/train cancellations. Bengaluru: occasional early-morning mist, rarely <1km.
sops.why_this_sop: Fog is the biggest WINTER travel hazard in North India; low visibility, not temperature, is the killer.
sops.advice_template:
Visibility is {visibility} m - dense fog. Travel is hazardous.
DRIVING:
- Delay non-essential travel until fog lifts (usually mid-morning)
- Use LOW-beam headlights + fog lights, never high beam (glare worsens it)
- Speed down to 20-40 km/h, keep large gap, follow lane markings not tail-lights
AIR/RAIL:
- Expect delays/cancellations; confirm status before leaving for airport/station
PEDESTRIANS:
- Wear light/reflective clothing; assume drivers cannot see you

sops.name: Cold Wave - Vulnerable Group Protection
sops.description: Temperature < 10 C (cold-wave risk for vulnerable groups on the plains)
sops.regional_context: North Indian plains (Delhi, UP, Bihar, Rajasthan) Dec-Jan. Distinct from frostbite (SOP-015, hill stations <-5 C): cold waves kill in the plains at 2-8 C via hypothermia in the elderly/homeless.
sops.why_this_sop: Elderly lose thermoregulation and thirst/cold sensation; kids lose heat faster. A '8 C' plains morning is life-threatening for them, not just uncomfortable.
sops.advice_template:
Temperature is {temperature_2m} C - cold-wave risk for vulnerable people.
ELDERLY (60+):
- Keep indoors during early morning/late night (coldest hours)
- Layer clothing; cover head, hands, feet; watch for confusion/slurred speech (hypothermia)
KIDS:
- Full layers before school; warm breakfast; no early-morning outdoor play
HEATING SAFETY:
- NEVER burn coal/braziers (angithi) in closed rooms - carbon-monoxide deaths are common in cold waves
- Keep a window slightly open if using any combustion heater

sops.name: Conditions Within Normal Limits
sops.description: No hazard policy triggered, and the user's outdoor activity is one this library covers
sops.regional_context: Applies anywhere. This is the 'nothing is wrong' branch, not a hazard rule.
sops.why_this_sop: Without this policy the library can only speak about hazards, so a mild day returned 'I have no guidance for that' -- which reads as broken and is not what the phrase is for. The brief reserves the honest no-match answer for questions no rule covers, not for covered activities in benign weather. This policy keeps the distinction: it fires only when the activity IS one we cover and no hazard policy fired. An activity outside the library still gets the honest no-match.
sops.advice_template:
GOOD TO GO

No safety policy in our library is triggered by the current conditions.

Live readings: temperature {temperature_2m} C (feels like {apparent_temperature} C), wind {wind_speed_10m} km/h, chance of rain {precipitation_probability}%, humidity {relative_humidity_2m}%.

Standard precautions still apply:
- Carry water and stay hydrated
- Check conditions again before you set out if that is more than an hour away
- Weather can change quickly; turn back if it does

metadata.note: All SOPs are independent JSON data. Adding new SOPs requires only JSON edit, no code changes. Each SOP has unique id and is fully traceable. Choose 12-15 SOPs for your implementation based on relevance to your region and demographic focus.

condition_grammar.note: One generic evaluator interprets this. Adding/altering any numeric OR compound SOP is a JSON edit only - no control-flow, weather-fetch, or model-call code is touched.

metadata.fetch_contract: weather.py fetches a fixed BROAD variable set (temperature_2m, apparent_temperature, wind_speed_10m, wind_gusts_10m, precipitation, precipitation_probability, precipitation_sum, snowfall_sum, weather_code, uv_index, relative_humidity_2m, visibility) so new policies over known metrics need zero code change. HONEST BOUNDARY: a policy needing a brand-new metric not in this list is the ONE case that requires adding that metric to the fetch list.
